subtitle: How Mihira Bhoja turned a boar into the mark of empire

panels.shot: dramatic close-up of a weathered Adivaraha coin floating over a hazy map of northern India
panels.action: Mihira Bhoja stands in shadow behind a magnified Adivaraha coin, its boar symbol gleaming against a vast, faintly sketched expanse of Kannauj, Rajasthan and Malwa trade routes.

dialogue.text: In Mihira Bhoja’s age of scarce silver and rival kings, a small billon coin bore a boar—and quietly bound devotion, power and trade into one.

i18n.hi: मिहिर भोज के कम चाँदी और दुश्मन राजाओं के दौर में, छोटे बिलन सिक्के पर बना वराह चुपचाप भक्ति, ताकत और व्यापार को एक कर रहा था।

panels.shot: slow push-in from high-angle view of bustling Kannauj into the royal mint complex
panels.action: A panoramic view of Kannauj’s crowded streets narrows toward a fortified mint courtyard, where Mihira Bhoja watches metal ingots carried past temple spires and caravan warehouses.

dialogue.text: When Mihira Bhoja ruled from Kannauj in the ninth century, his power stretched far, but silver to fuel that power did not.

i18n.hi: नवें शताब्दी में जब मिहिर भोज कन्नौज से राज करता था, उसका असर दूर तक था, पर उस ताकत को चलाने वाली चाँदी नहीं थी।

panels.shot: medium shot inside the mint, low-angle on furnaces and workers
panels.action: Inside the mint, artisans tend glowing furnaces, pouring pale molten metal into molds, while Mihira Bhoja stands observant, hand on sword, amid stacked bars of mixed alloys.

dialogue.text: Across northern India, tribute, land grants and barter shared space with coins of mixed metal, billon, born from an age ‘living without silver’.

i18n.hi: पूरा उत्तर भारत नज़राना, ज़मीन दान और बदलाबदल से चलता, साथ में मिला-जुला धातु — बिलन — के सिक्के, एक ‘बिन चाँदी’ के युग की पैदाइश।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Mihira Bhoja’s thoughtful face catching the glow of a furnace
panels.action: Mihira Bhoja’s face is lit by orange furnace light, eyes narrowed in calculation as a worker presents a small, dull-gray blank flan on a pair of tongs.

dialogue.text: Mihira Bhoja inherited an empire and a problem: how to give this base metal a value that men would trust—and remember.

i18n.hi: मिहिर भोज को मिला साम्राज्य और सिरदर्द: इस घटिया धातु को ऐसी कीमत कैसे दें कि लोग उस पर भरोसा भी करें, याद भी रखें।

panels.shot: tabletop overhead shot of design sketches and older coins from northwest India
panels.action: On a wooden table lie sketch-plates of a boar, Sanskrit letters, and a row of worn Sasanian-style coins with a ruler’s bust and fire altar, as Mihira Bhoja’s hand hovers over them.

dialogue.text: Older coins from the northwest carried Sasanian forms—a facing bust, a stylized altar—traces of a wider world of money flowing into Pratihara lands.

i18n.hi: पुराने सिक्कों पर उत्तर-पश्चिम से आए सासानी आकार थे— सामने मुखाकृति, शैलीदार वेदी—पृथ्विहारा भूमि में घुसते बड़े पैमाने की मुद्रा-धारा के निशान।

panels.shot: symbolic close-up of a Varaha icon carved in a temple and a sketch mirroring it
panels.action: A stone relief of Vishnu’s Varaha lifting the earth disc in a temple wall is mirrored by a parchment sketch of the same boar form, placed beside mint tools.

dialogue.text: In his temples, Varaha, Vishnu’s boar, raised the earth from chaos. On his drawing board, that cosmic rescue became a political idea.

i18n.hi: उसके मंदिरों में विष्णु का वराह धरती को अराजकता से ऊपर उठाता था। उसकी मेज़ पर वही ब्रह्मांडीय उद्धार एक राजनीतिक चाल बन गया।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot as Mihira Bhoja addresses his mint officials
panels.action: In the mint hall, Mihira Bhoja stands firm, gesturing toward a clay model of a coin showing the boar, while seated officials and engravers listen intently.

dialogue.speaker: mihira_bhoja
dialogue.text: Let every payment bear witness: the earth stands rescued, and ordered, under our care.

i18n.hi: हर भुगतान गवाह बने: धरती बच चुकी है, सँवारी जा चुकी है, हमारे अधिकार में सुरक्षित है।

panels.shot: close-up of an engraved die with the legend and boar about to strike a blank
panels.action: An engraver’s hand positions a die bearing the boar and the legend in clear Nagari, poised above a blank billon flan on an anvil, Mihira Bhoja’s shadow falling across it.

dialogue.text: The new drammas bore Varaha and the title ‘Śrīmad Ādivarāha’—casting the king as the auspicious, primal boar who steadied the earth.

i18n.hi: नए ड्रम्मों पर वराह और उपाधि ‘श्रीमद आदिवराह’ उकेरी गई—राजा को शुभ, आदिकालीन वराह के रूप में गढ़ती, जो धरती को स्थिर रखता है।

panels.shot: freeze-frame close shot as the hammer descends on the coin flan
panels.action: A heavy hammer is frozen mid-strike above the die and flan, sparks ready to fly, capturing the instant before the boar’s image is impressed into metal.

dialogue.text: With each blow of the die, theology hardened into currency. Devotion and authority sank together into the alloy.

i18n.hi: हर चोट के साथ, धर्मशास्त्र सिक्के में जम गया। भक्ति और सत्ता एक साथ उस मिश्रधातु में धँस गईं।

panels.shot: double-sided macro view of an Adivaraha coin hovering, obverse and reverse visible
panels.action: The Adivaraha coin is shown in crisp detail: one face with Varaha and legend, the other echoing Sasanian forms—a stylized bust and altar—floating against a neutral background.

dialogue.text: One face proclaimed Varaha and Bhoja’s title. The other kept familiar, Sasanian-derived shapes, tying Pratihara money to old northwest routes.

i18n.hi: एक तरफ वराह और भोज की उपाधि चमकती थी। दूसरी तरफ पुराने, सासानी रूप बने रहे, पृथ्विहारा मुद्रा को उत्तर-पश्चिम की पुरानी राहों से बाँधते हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of caravan routes with traders exchanging Adivaraha coins
panels.action: Across dusty roads, camel caravans and bullock carts halt as traders in varied dress pass Adivaraha coins from palm to palm amid sacks of grain and textiles.

dialogue.text: From Kannauj to Rajasthan and Malwa, the new drammas moved with cloth, salt and horses, weaving the king’s symbol into everyday exchange.

i18n.hi: कन्नौज से राजस्थान और मालवा तक नए ड्रम्मे कपड़ा, नमक और घोड़ों के साथ चलते गए, राजा की निशानी को रोजमर्रा के सौदे में बुनते हुए।

panels.shot: intimate close shot of hands using coins alongside barter and gift
panels.action: A village scene shows one pair of hands counting Adivaraha coins, another weighing grain, and a third offering a wrapped gift, all in the same courtyard.

dialogue.text: Coins did not replace land grants, barter or ceremonial gifts. They stood beside them—suited for markets, taxes, soldiers’ wages and distant tribute.

i18n.hi: सिक्के ने ज़मीन दान, बदलाबदल या रस्मी उपहार को नहीं हटाया। वे उनके साथ खड़े रहे—हाट-बाज़ार, लगान, सैनिकों की मज़दूरी और दूर-दराज़ के नज़राने के लिए ठीक बैठे।

panels.shot: low-angle wide shot of Mihira Bhoja presiding over courtly tribute
panels.action: In a grand audience hall, Mihira Bhoja sits on a high throne as envoys lay chests of coin, rolls of cloth and ledgers at his feet in a formal act of submission.

dialogue.text: Each chest of Adivaraha drammas offered by feudatories did more than pay dues—it repeated his claim to rescue and rule, without a word spoken.

i18n.hi: जागीरदारों की भेंट में भरे हर आदिवराह ड्रम्मों के संदूक ने सिर्फ लगान नहीं चुकाया—बिना बोले ही उसके ‘उद्धार और राज’ के दावे को दोहराया।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composition of coins aging, passed through many hands
panels.action: Several Adivaraha coins are shown in stages of wear—from sharp to smoothed—overlapping as if moving through time, with ghostly hands of different communities reaching for them.

dialogue.text: Over decades, the silver content thinned, legends blurred, yet the boar’s outline endured, carrying its message as the metal itself grew humble.

i18n.hi: दशकों बीते, चाँदी कम होती गई, लेख धुँधले पड़ते गए, पर वराह की परछाईं टिके रही—अपना संदेश उठाए, जबकि खुद धातु और भी मामूली हो गई।

panels.shot: medieval library interior as Thakkar Pheru studies and classifies coins
panels.action: In a later, thirteenth-century setting, mint-master Thakkar Pheru sits among scrolls, examining an old Adivaraha coin with a lens, while noting its type on a palm-leaf manuscript.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, Thakkar Pheru’s Dravya-Pariksha still recognized these Varaha pieces, proof that Bhoja’s design had marked the memory of India’s money.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद ठक्कर फेरू की ‘द्रव्य-परिक्षा’ इन वराह सिक्कों को अब भी पहचानती है—सबूत कि भोज की डिज़ाइन ने भारत की मुद्रा की स्मृति पर छाप छोड़ दी।

panels.shot: modern scholarly desk with Deyell’s book open beside coins and maps
panels.action: A contemporary scholar’s desk shows John Deyell’s volume open to diagrams of billon circulation, Adivaraha coins laid out on a map of early medieval trade regions.

dialogue.text: Modern study of ‘living without silver’ reveals the strain behind these coins: they answered shortage with alloy, icon and habit, not with pure bullion.

i18n.hi: ‘बिना चाँदी के जीने’ पर आधुनिक अध्ययन दिखाते हैं कि इन सिक्कों के पीछे कितना दबाव था: कमी का जवाब शुद्ध चाँदी से नहीं, मिश्रधातु, चिन्ह और आदत से दिया गया।

panels.shot: symbolic wide shot blending temple, court, and marketplace around Bhoja
panels.action: Mihira Bhoja stands at the center of a composite scene where a temple with Varaha relief, a royal court, and a bustling bazaar all radiate outward, Adivaraha coins glinting between them.

dialogue.text: In Mihira Bhoja’s world, the same small disc linked shrine, throne and stall. The boar on the coin made faith, sovereignty and trade share a single face.

i18n.hi: मिहिर भोज की दुनिया में यही छोटा चक्का मंदिर, सिंहासन और बाज़ार की दुकान को जोड़ता था। सिक्के पर बना वराह ही श्रद्धा, सत्ता और व्यापार को एक चेहरा देता था।

panels.shot: final contemplative close-up of a single worn Adivaraha coin resting in an open palm
panels.action: A solitary, worn Adivaraha coin lies in a human palm against a plain background, its faint boar still visible, the hand relaxed and thoughtful.

dialogue.text: Seen now, the Adivaraha drammas remind us: money is never mute. It carries the stories rulers choose to stamp into the metal of everyday life.

i18n.hi: आज इन्हें देखते हुए आदिवराह ड्रम्मे याद दिलाते हैं: पैसा कभी गूंगा नहीं होता। उसमें वही कहानियाँ दर्ज रहती हैं जिन्हें शासक रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी की धातु पर ठप्पा मारना चुनते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: How Mihira Bhoja turned a boar into the mark of empire
subtitle_i18n.hi: कैसे मिहिर भोज ने वराह को साम्राज्य की पहचान बना दिया
